sentence: 'The caller hung up before I could explain the new charges.'
setupText: Choose the interpretation supported by the account.
taskText: 'The caller hung up before I could explain the new charges.'
text: Choose the interpretation supported by the account. 'The caller hung up before I could explain the new charges.'
options: The explanation caused the caller to hang up.
The speaker completed the explanation and then the call ended.
The speaker deliberately ended the call to avoid explaining.
The call ended before the speaker had the opportunity to explain.
answer: The call ended before the speaker had the opportunity to explain.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-b2-541:Before could and a prevented opportunity
explanation: Before I could marks an opportunity cut short by the earlier end of the call.

rationales.The explanation caused the caller to han: The explanation had not occurred, so it is not given as the cause of hanging up.
rationales.The call ended before the speaker had th: Before I could marks an opportunity cut short by the earlier end of the call.
rationales.The speaker completed the explanation an: This reverses the sequence and asserts an explanation the original says was not possible in time.
rationales.The speaker deliberately ended the call: The caller ended the call; the speaker does not claim to have avoided the explanation deliberately.

sentence: 'The gallery did not reopen until the repairs were complete.'
setupText: Choose the rewrite preserving that reopening waited for completed repairs.
taskText: 'The gallery did not reopen until the repairs were complete.'
text: Choose the rewrite preserving that reopening waited for completed repairs. 'The gallery did not reopen until the repairs were complete.'
options: The gallery reopened while repairs were still in progress.
The gallery reopened even though repairs were incomplete.
The gallery reopened only after the repairs were complete.
The gallery completed the repairs after reopening.
answer: The gallery reopened only after the repairs were complete.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-b2-542:Not until paraphrased as only after
explanation: Only after preserves the delay up to completion expressed by did not ... until.

rationales.The gallery reopened while repairs were: While repairs were in progress removes the completed-repair requirement.
rationales.The gallery reopened even though repairs: This explicitly allows reopening despite incomplete repairs, contrary to the source.
rationales.The gallery reopened only after the repa: Only after preserves the delay up to completion expressed by did not ... until.
rationales.The gallery completed the repairs after: This places reopening first and repairs later, reversing the required order.

explanation: In spite of explicitly concedes the cost as a drawback that did not prevent approval.

rationales.In view of: In view of presents cost as a consideration supporting the decision, rather than marking an obstacle overcome.
rationales.On account of: On account of makes the cost the reason for approving.
rationales.As a result of: As a result of makes approval a consequence of the cost.
rationales.In spite of: In spite of explicitly concedes the cost as a drawback that did not prevent approval.

sentence: 'The form was redesigned so that applicants could complete it without assistance.'
setupText: Choose what the purpose clause establishes without assuming the plan succeeded.
taskText: 'The form was redesigned so that applicants could complete it without assistance.'
text: Choose what the purpose clause establishes without assuming the plan succeeded. 'The form was redesigned so that applicants could complete it without assistance.'
options: Independent completion was the aim of the redesign.
Applicants became able to complete it without help as an achieved result.
Applicants had already completed it independently before it was redesigned.
Applicants' independent completion caused the redesign.
answer: Independent completion was the aim of the redesign.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-b2-545:Purpose does not guarantee achievement
explanation: So that applicants could states the intended benefit; it does not by itself report measured success.

rationales.Applicants became able to complete it wi: The purpose clause states the intended benefit; it does not by itself establish that the redesign achieved it.
rationales.Applicants had already completed it inde: The clause presents independent completion as the redesign's goal, not a reported prior achievement.
rationales.Independent completion was the aim of th: So that applicants could states the intended benefit; it does not by itself report measured success.
rationales.Applicants' independent completion cause: This reverses the direction, turning the intended benefit into a prior cause.

sentence: The team combined the two delivery routes, ___ reducing fuel use.

focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-b2-546:Thereby connects a means to its consequence
explanation: Thereby connects the action to an effect achieved through that action.

rationales.nevertheless: 'Nevertheless' marks an unexpected contrast, not a result achieved by the route change.
rationales.thereby: Thereby connects the action to an effect achieved through that action.
rationales.otherwise: 'Otherwise' describes a different situation or other respects, not the stated effect of combining routes.

explanation: Even so acknowledges the careful preparation while introducing an outcome contrary to expectation.

rationales.Accordingly: Accordingly would make failure an expected result of the preparation.
rationales.For that reason: For that reason explicitly presents rehearsal as the cause of failure.

rationales.Even so: Even so acknowledges the careful preparation while introducing an outcome contrary to expectation.

sentence: The sentence 'As the manager was away, I handled the complaint' could be read in more than one way. The writer intends the manager's absence as the reason.
setupText: Choose the rewrite that unambiguously gives a reason, not a simultaneous time.
taskText: The sentence 'As the manager was away, I handled the complaint' could be read in more than one way. The writer intends the manager's absence as the reason.
text: Choose the rewrite that unambiguously gives a reason, not a simultaneous time. The sentence 'As the manager was away, I handled the complaint' could be read in more than one way. The writer intends the manager's absence as the reason.
options: While the manager was away, I handled the complaint.
When the manager was away, I handled the complaint.
Throughout the manager's absence, I handled the complaint.
Because the manager was away, I handled the complaint.
answer: Because the manager was away, I handled the complaint.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-b2-550:Disambiguating causal as
explanation: Because directly identifies the absence as the reason for taking responsibility.

rationales.While the manager was away, I handled th: While explicitly highlights the shared period and may retain ambiguity about the intended relationship.
rationales.Because the manager was away, I handled: Because directly identifies the absence as the reason for taking responsibility.
rationales.When the manager was away, I handled the: When specifies a time and does not explicitly state the causal link.
rationales.Throughout the manager's absence, I hand: 'Throughout' describes duration over the absence rather than identifying the reason.

sentence: 'I stayed on the call as long as my battery lasted, then continued by email.'
setupText: Choose the meaning of 'as long as' in this account.
taskText: 'I stayed on the call as long as my battery lasted, then continued by email.'
text: Choose the meaning of 'as long as' in this account. 'I stayed on the call as long as my battery lasted, then continued by email.'
options: The speaker stayed on the call for the duration of the battery's remaining power.
The battery lasting was an unconfirmed condition for joining the call.
The call was shorter because email was available.
The speaker stayed on the call after the battery ran out.
answer: The speaker stayed on the call for the duration of the battery's remaining power.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-b2-551:Durational as long as
explanation: 'As long as' describes the whole period during which the battery continued to supply power.

rationales.The battery lasting was an unconfirmed c: The speaker reports an actual duration, not an unresolved condition for joining.
rationales.The call was shorter because email was a: No shorter alternative duration is stated; the battery sets the limit.
rationales.The speaker stayed on the call for the d: 'As long as' describes the whole period during which the battery continued to supply power.
rationales.The speaker stayed on the call after the: 'Then continued by email' indicates a change when the battery no longer supported the call.

taskText: The delay arose from poor coordination ___ a shortage of staff.

explanation: Rather than favors poor coordination over the alternative explanation of staff shortage.

rationales.as well as: As well as includes both explanations instead of setting one aside.
rationales.rather than: Rather than favors poor coordination over the alternative explanation of staff shortage.
rationales.in addition to: In addition to adds staff shortage as another contributing factor.
rationales.together with: Together with likewise presents the two factors jointly rather than contrasting explanations.

sentence: 'We left early, not because the speaker was boring, but because our train was leaving.'
setupText: Choose the inference supported by the correction of reasons.
taskText: 'We left early, not because the speaker was boring, but because our train was leaving.'
text: Choose the inference supported by the correction of reasons. 'We left early, not because the speaker was boring, but because our train was leaving.'
options: The listeners did not find the speaker boring.
The train schedule is given as the reason for leaving early.
Both boredom and the train schedule motivated the departure.
The listeners left because the talk had ended.
answer: The train schedule is given as the reason for leaving early.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-b2-553:Correcting a cause without negating every underlying fact
explanation: Not because ... but because corrects the proposed explanation while keeping the early departure as fact.

rationales.The listeners did not find the speaker b: Denying boredom as the reason for leaving does not determine whether they found the speaker boring.
rationales.Both boredom and the train schedule moti: Not because explicitly rejects boredom as a motive; the causes are not being added together.
rationales.The listeners left because the talk had: The sentence says they left early and identifies the train schedule, not the end of the talk, as the reason.
rationales.The train schedule is given as the reaso: Not because ... but because corrects the proposed explanation while keeping the early departure as fact.

sentence: Staff turnover fell because the company introduced flexible shifts.
setupText: Choose the sentence preserving the stated direction of cause and effect.
taskText: Staff turnover fell because the company introduced flexible shifts.
text: Choose the sentence preserving the stated direction of cause and effect. Staff turnover fell because the company introduced flexible shifts.
options: The company introduced flexible shifts as a result of falling staff turnover.
The introduction of flexible shifts led to a fall in staff turnover.
Falling staff turnover led the company to introduce flexible shifts.
The company introduced flexible shifts despite a fall in staff turnover.
answer: The introduction of flexible shifts led to a fall in staff turnover.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-b2-559:Preserving causality across clause and noun-phrase forms
explanation: Led to preserves flexible shifts as the cause and lower turnover as the effect.

rationales.The company introduced flexible shifts a: This makes falling turnover the cause of the shift change, reversing the source.
rationales.Falling staff turnover led the company t: This also reverses which event caused the other.
rationales.The introduction of flexible shifts led: Led to preserves flexible shifts as the cause and lower turnover as the effect.
rationales.The company introduced flexible shifts d: Despite turns the causal relationship into a concession.

sentence: 'The results cannot be released until Monday, but they must be released by Wednesday.'

taskText: 'The results cannot be released until Monday, but they must be released by Wednesday.'
text: Choose the interpretation that respects both time limits. 'The results cannot be released until Monday, but they must be released by Wednesday.'
options: Release may occur from Monday through Wednesday, subject to those limits.
Release is required on Wednesday and no other day.
Release must continue without interruption from Monday to Wednesday.
Release must happen before Monday or after Wednesday.
answer: Release may occur from Monday through Wednesday, subject to those limits.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-b2-560:Earliest point with until versus deadline with by
explanation: Until Monday sets the earliest point and by Wednesday the deadline, leaving the interval between them.

rationales.Release is required on Wednesday and no: By Wednesday sets the latest time, not the only permitted day.
rationales.Release may occur from Monday through We: Until Monday sets the earliest point and by Wednesday the deadline, leaving the interval between them.
rationales.Release must continue without interrupti: These clauses constrain the timing of the release event; they do not describe a continuous activity.
rationales.Release must happen before Monday or aft: This selects times outside both stated boundaries.
